speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you tell me more about the feeding difficulties, such as whether the baby spits up frequently or seems in pain during feeds? Also, has the baby passed stool regularly, and if so, what does it look like?

speaker: Patient
text: The baby has been very fussy, feeding less than usual, and the abdomen looks distended. Crying gets worse when the belly is touched.

speaker: Doctor
text: Has the baby had any episodes of vomiting, and if so, is the vomit green or yellow? Also, when was the last time he passed a stool, and what was its consistency?

speaker: Patient
text: There has not been fever, vomiting, or diarrhea like a stomach infection. The baby was born at 39 weeks without birth complications.

speaker: Doctor
text: Has the baby passed any meconium in the first 48 hours of life, and does his stool typically appear thin and ribbon-like? I am also going to perform a digital rectal examination to check for tightness or a sudden release of stool and gas.

speaker: Patient
text: The baby did not seem to pass stool normally and the belly swelling has become more obvious. Feeding has clearly decreased over the past few days.

speaker: Doctor
text: I will perform a digital rectal examination to assess for a tight anal sphincter and a sudden release of stool or gas. REQUEST TEST: Abdominal X-Ray.

speaker: Doctor
text: The X-ray findings of dilated bowel with a gasless rectum, combined with delayed meconium passage and abdominal distension, are highly suggestive of Hirschsprung disease. To confirm the diagnosis and identify the transition zone, I will request a contrast enema. REQUEST TEST: Contrast Enema.
